note: ADR premise probes. An ADR's load-bearing premise is a claim about the code; a probe is the cheapest mechanical restatement of that claim, and it fails when the code drifts away from the decision. Enforced by the adr-coverage kernel gate (rule adr-coverage/probe-failed). Referenced from each ADR's frontmatter as 'probes: [<id>]'. When a probe fails, the fix is to re-examine and amend the ADR per docs/decisions/README.md - never to edit the probe until it passes. Kinds in preference order (tempdoc 884 design decision 2): test/gate first (a named test or an existing enforcement already IS the probe), then absence probes, then counts - and counts only where the premise IS the count (ADR-0015 is the one).
amendmentProcedure: docs/decisions/README.md § How to re-examine an ADR

probes.premise: Application code never touches Lucene: only adapters-lucene and the index half (indexerworker) may depend on Lucene classes. RETARGETED from adr-0001-lucene-owners-pinned at lane F item A15. The property is unchanged and the test is unchanged -- only its owning decision moved, because ADR-0001 is superseded. Sharing an address space does not license reaching past a port into the index, which is precisely why this pin matters MORE after the merge than before it: while the Head was a separate process the boundary was also enforced by the OS.
probes.note: Not weakened by the merge. ADR-0049 carries the class-level Lucene-owner pin verbatim; the PROCESS half of ADR-0001 invariant 1 became ArchUnit rule 6b, which has its own probe (adr-0049-engine-port-boundary) rather than being folded into this one -- two properties, two probes.

probes.premise: Only the Engine composition root, the index half itself and the Lucene adapters may reach into the index half’s internals. This is the process half of ADR-0001 invariant 1, re-expressed as a module boundary now that there is no process boundary to carry it: rule 6b permits io.justsearch.app.engine.., io.justsearch.indexerworker.. and io.justsearch.adapters.. to depend on io.justsearch.indexerworker.{server,services,loop}.., and nothing else. Losing it means application code can call the index half directly, which is the drift one address space makes possible and two did not.
probes.note: Added at lane F item A15. Complements the engine-port register (governance/engine-ports.v1.json + the engine-port gate), which guards the other direction: this stops code reaching PAST a port, the register stops a second implementation claiming to BE one.

probes.premise: NO module build file declares a gRPC dependency. REPLACES adr-0002-grpc-present, inverted: that probe asserted gRPC was PRESENT because the hybrid IPC depended on it, so the honest successor is an absence probe (this register preference order puts absence above counts). Item A14 removed the last declaration anywhere under modules/, including the infra-health service that had been the one exemption, so the scope is the whole tree rather than the index half alone. A libs.grpc line reappearing in ANY module build means the deleted channel is being rebuilt.
probes.note: Added at lane F item A15, widened to all of modules/ at A14. It was briefly scoped to worker-core/worker-services/indexer-worker while the infra-health gRPC service was expected to survive; the owner then decided that service is part of the wire and it was deleted, so the exemption is gone and the probe means the simpler thing. Note that grep-absent counts COMMENTS as well as code, and that is deliberate here: a comment naming libs.grpc is residue by the same rule that deleted the dependency, and the probe caught exactly one such comment in modules/indexer-worker/build.gradle.kts before it passed.

probes.premise: NO Java source under modules/ imports io.grpc. The build-file probe above is necessary and not sufficient: it watches the DECLARATION, and a declaration can return by a route that does not spell 'libs.grpc' - a transitive edge, a version-catalog alias, a direct coordinate string. What ADR-0049 actually decided is that no gRPC method is served and no gRPC type crosses a seam, and the cheapest mechanical restatement of THAT is the import statement, which is where a returning dependency first becomes visible in code.
probes.note: Added at the lane F stage A checkpoint. Anchored to a line start deliberately, and this is the one place it differs from its build-file sibling: that probe counts comments on purpose (a comment naming libs.grpc is residue), whereas io.grpc is still NAMED in prose all over the tree - GplJobCoordinator, AgentToolErrors, KnowledgeClientException and CancelToken all explain in javadoc which io.grpc type they used to match, and those explanations are the record of the retargeting, not residue. An unanchored pattern would have to delete that history to go green, which is the wrong trade. Main AND test sources are in scope: a test importing io.grpc means a gRPC artifact is back on a test classpath, which is how the dependency returns before anyone ships it.

probes.premise: Lucene is consumed as a library directly.
No search platform (Elasticsearch / OpenSearch / Solr) is a dependency.
Backfill yields the GPU when Main has claimed it, and the energy reason stays distinct from the VRAM-conflict reason.
The CPU cross-encoder prong is wired: the search service owns a CitationScorer and exposes post-hoc citation matching.

The post-hoc prong is reached from the search path: matchCitations delegates to CitationMatchOps, which owns the CitationScorer. A CitationScorer class that nothing calls would satisfy the ADR's letter and not its decision.

ADR-0007 chose entity FACETS over a knowledge graph. Faceting shipped and is live; decision-review lane D C0 retired the separate entity_*_text query boost and its configuration, while C2 removes the now-unqueried physical text fields. The premise this probe pins is 'the entity boost is retired' throughout that two-step migration.
probes.note: Two alternatives, one premise across a planned migration. In C0 alternative 1 proves the functional configuration and query machinery are absent while the physical entity_*_text fields remain for C2. After C2, alternative 2 additionally proves catalog absence. The protobuf/status entityBoost compatibility tombstone is deliberately outside the scanned paths and remains field 9, always projected as 0.0. This is NOT a probe that gives a failure a second chance: BOTH failing means query machinery returned while the physical fields exist — exactly the drift to catch.

probes.premise: An incompatible settings file is replaced with defaults and the reset is surfaced as a lifecycle condition, not swallowed.
The reset carries a named lifecycle reason code (SETTINGS_RESET_FROM_CORRUPT).

The Remote Shard SPI was never built and the ADR was retired on 2026-09-02 (status 'rejected - never built'). The absence is now the decision: a single-user desktop product has no shard need, so no RemoteShard symbol may exist in shipped code. Building one fails this probe and forces a deliberate ADR change first.

The MCP surface is a small curated tool list, because small models pick badly from long lists. The count IS the decision: the canonical production ToolDefinition registry has 6 tools (answer, search, browse, ingest, status, runtime_manifest).
Query-understanding signals enter the query as soft boosts: both boost sites wrap the clause in BoostQuery(ConstantScoreQuery(...)) so the boost cannot vary with IDF.
probes.note: The count is the whole boost population (term boost + range boost), not a growth ratchet: a third boost site is a deliberate ADR-0016 decision about what may be soft-boosted, so it should land with an ADR read.

probes.premise: Never apply QU output as a hard filter: a BoostQuery must never be added on a FILTER or MUST clause, which would exclude non-matching documents instead of ranking them lower.
The ai-bridge monolith was split into ai-backend, gpu-bridge and prompt-support.
ai-bridge, app-ai and ai-worker were deleted, not left behind.

The ADR's 2026-09-02 amendment records that JUSTSEARCH_LAYOUT_ENABLED does not exist: the enable flag named in the original Decision section never shipped (or was removed), and VDU/VLM routing is default-on, per-extension, inside a tiered extraction-fallback budget. Re-introducing the flag name means the routing decision changed and this ADR must be re-decided, not re-gated.
API records get their fluent builders from the io.soabase record-builder annotation processor, so fields can evolve additively.
The NSIS bundle installs per-user (currentUser), non-elevated — the decision that makes post-install model download into LocalAppData work without UAC.
probes.note: This probe covers the CONFIG assertion only. scripts/ci/check-installer-execution-level.mjs — uninvoked when 884 §F row 7 routed it, now wired into ci.yml (config half + its unit test) and build-installer.yml's installer_verify job (artifact half) — additionally byte-scans the BUILT installer's embedded manifest, which is the half this json-path cannot see: an installer-hooks.nsh change can leave installMode correct while the shipped setup.exe still requests elevation.

probes.premise: Self-hosted and specialty workflows stay manually dispatched; the trigger policy is machine-checked, not remembered.

Exactly ONE HTTP entry point may resolve a path hash. The approved-caller allowlist contains exactly one io.justsearch.ui.api Controller (IndexingController, which owns POST /api/library/resolve-hash); a second one is the privacy-contract change the ADR exists to make deliberate.
The durable identity table is hash-keyed and has no raw-path column; its exact schema is pinned by a runnable migration test.

ADR-0029 is a criteria ADR: it tells the next MetricCatalog adopter which of TWO shipped idioms to pick. The bridge idiom must still exist for that choice to be real — a domain-owned *TelemetryEvents interface implemented by an adapter in a module that may depend on the catalog package. The three shipped bridge instances are WorkerLuceneTelemetryAdapter, OrtSessionTelemetryAdapter and EmbeddingTelemetry.
probes.note: The count is the named bridge population, not a growth ratchet: `paths` lists exactly the three files ADR-0029 cites as its bridge instances, so a FOURTH bridge elsewhere in the tree does not move this number. It fails when one of the three stops implementing a *TelemetryEvents interface — i.e. when the bridge idiom is being converted away, which is the drift that makes a two-idiom criteria ADR moot.

probes.premise: The other half of ADR-0029's choice: the direct-emit facade idiom — a thin Telemetry class holding catalog instruments directly, implementing NO events interface. The two shipped instances are AgentTelemetry (over AgentMetricCatalog + GenAiMetricCatalog) and IpcTelemetry (over IpcMetricCatalog).
probes.note: The count is the named direct-emit population, not a growth ratchet: `paths` lists exactly the two files ADR-0029 cites, so a third direct-emit facade elsewhere does not move it. The literal `{` after the class name is the discriminator — converting either class to the bridge idiom (`... implements XxxTelemetryEvents {`) drops the count and fails the probe, which is exactly when a two-idiom criteria ADR should be re-read.

probes.premise: The Operation-policy divergence is delivered where the code is edited: a consult-register region points the agent at this ADR.
The frontend is Lit web components; the React stack is retired, not dormant.
Resource carries a typed Category axis, and operator-trace data is not Resource truth — the boundary is gate-enforced.

Hand-written mirrors of the wire contract are forbidden: every consumer-side type under modules/ui-web/src is either mechanically generated (registered in governance/contract-surfaces.v1.json) or a declared, reasoned exception. The ADR's own Rationale names three drift sites -- api/domains/*, shell-v0/handshake/capabilities-types.ts and api/schemas.ts -- so the scan is the whole source tree, not one directory.

exceptions.reason: DECLARED EXCEPTION, owner: the UI lane. Hand-written mirror of ConversationShape/ConversationShapeRef (slice 491 section 9.D) -- structurally the same case surface.ts just resolved (a plain record projection the existing emitter can express), so the fix is the surface.ts recipe applied again: add a captureOrVerify case to SubstrateSchemaGenTest, a TARGETS entry, a contract-surfaces record, and reduce this file to a composing barrel. Not done in tempdoc 884 PR 2 because ConversationShape's FE consumers carry client-side state the wire does not, and re-shaping them is modules/ui-web component work, which lane B does not own. Recorded per the ADR-0038 amendment 2026-09-02.

DECLARED EXCEPTION, owner: the UI lane. Hand-written mirror of the Java sealed sums under app-api/selection (tempdoc 526). Unlike surface.ts this one is BLOCKED, not merely unscheduled: sealed-sum discriminated unions are not expressible by the record-to-JSON-Schema-to-TS emitter (gen-wire-schema-types.mjs supports type/properties/required/items/enum/const/anyOf and $ref into #/$defs; it has no discriminator concept). Generating it requires extending the emitter first. Recorded per the ADR-0038 amendment 2026-09-02.

DECLARED EXCEPTION, owner: the UI lane. Hand-written TS view of the /infra/capabilities payload, self-declared at :3-10 as mirroring CapabilitiesService.CapabilitiesView in modules/app-observability, and absent from contract-surfaces.v1.json. Same recipe as surface.ts (CapabilitiesView is a plain record), but the handshake payload is consumed during boot before the generated-module graph is loaded, so the migration has an ordering question lane B did not investigate. Recorded per the ADR-0038 amendment 2026-09-02.

DECLARED EXCEPTION, owner: the UI lane. Carries no mirror marker but is one, and the drift runs BACKWARDS: ApplyExcludesResponse/PatternMatch (:95,:100) are mirrored FROM the FE by ExcludesService.ExcludesResult (modules/.../ExcludesService.java:35-38 says so in its javadoc). Generating it would invert the authority, which is a product decision about who owns the excludes contract, not a codegen chore. Recorded per the ADR-0038 amendment 2026-09-02.

DECLARED EXCEPTION, owner: the UI lane. Named by ADR-0038's Rationale as the hand-written Zod half of the drift; tempdoc 683 already reduced it to ONE deliberately permissive .loose() agent-session schema, and the rest now validate against generated projections. The residue is a deliberate fail-open parse boundary, so retiring it is a decision about that boundary rather than a mirror to generate. Recorded per the ADR-0038 amendment 2026-09-02.
Marker false positive, not a mirror: :27 says this USED to be a hand-written mirror, retired by tempdoc 840 Phase 4. Listed so the marker scan stays green without weakening the regex.

probes.note: registry.ts and diagnostic.ts need no exception -- both appear in governance/contract-surfaces.v1.json as declared consumers of generated projections, and as of tempdoc 884 PR 2 so does api/types/surface.ts, which is now a composing barrel over the generated SurfaceWire rather than a mirror (its exception was dropped in the same change -- the probe fails on a stale exception, so that handshake was mechanical). The probe scans every .ts under modules/ui-web/src (excluding generated/, tests and fixtures) for a self-declared mirror marker; a marked file must be registered or excepted. Unmarked mirrors are invisible to the scan by construction, which is why the two known ones (indexing.ts, schemas.ts) are declared here explicitly. Every remaining exception names its blocker and its owner: the ADR-0038 amendment of 2026-09-02 is the record, not this list.

probes.premise: Narrowed by the ADR's 2026-09-02 amendment: ADR-0039 decides the contract substrate for exactly the one Category that exists, wire. The plugin-SDK, catalog and registry-serialization Categories its Decision section names were never registered and are not decided by the ADR. A second entry in /categories reopens it — the Category must be decided here before it is registered.

Consumer presence is checked over the LIVE ContributionRegistry, not only the static snapshot, and that live check reuses the build-tier consumer merge rather than forking it. Tempdoc 930 (2026-09-05) retired the live-witness register and its offline wiring check; the enforcing test is the sole authority, so this probe points at it directly.
No per-language analysis artifact (analyzer field, stopwords, spelling dictionary, curated synonyms) may be authored; analysis is locale-invariant.
Public hosted CI runs on push and pull request in stable fact lanes; every workflow's trigger set is policy-checked.
The required npm lockfile advisory fact uses bounded GitHub Global Advisory requests and identity-based regression tests rather than npm's bulk POST or aggregate counts.
Public main receives curated squash commits only; the repository's history-publication settings are machine-checked.
The PR title/body remain commit-safe public input while one separately managed PR comment carries head/body-bound mutable review evidence; the publication command remains present.
The managed review-record regression stays invoked by hosted CI.
The repository-owned agent enqueue gateway validates the live public squash and managed review records before requesting the merge queue, and its fail-closed regression stays invoked by hosted CI.
Ordinary direct agent CLI merge commands are refused in favor of the validated enqueue gateway, and the cross-harness guard regression stays invoked by hosted CI.

The whole trust boundary rests on the network being unable to reach the port: the local API's bind address is the literal 127.0.0.1, not a setting. There is no configuration path to 0.0.0.0. Binding anything else voids ADR-0046 until it is re-derived.
probes.note: expect 1 is the population, not a ratchet: there is exactly one bind call site. The pattern requires the 'this.app.' receiver so it pins the real call and not the javadoc at the same file's :773, which quotes 'app.start("127.0.0.1", bindPort)' as prose.

probes.premise: The bind address is never widened to a wildcard. ADR-0046's whole control set assumes the network cannot reach the port, so a start() on 0.0.0.0 voids the decision rather than extending it.
probes.note: Scoped to the start() CALL, not the bare address: the file's javadoc at :774 and :811 deliberately discusses what a 0.0.0.0 bind would expose, and evaluateGrep does not strip comments, so a bare-address absence probe would go red on the prose that exists to warn against the very thing it checks. Paired with adr-0046-loopback-bind-literal, which pins the positive side.

probes.premise: Session-token enforcement fails CLOSED: prod mode with a null or blank token refuses to construct the API and raises LOCAL_API_SESSION_TOKEN_MISSING, rather than logging that enforcement is disabled and serving mutations unguarded. HONEST LIMIT: this probe is kind 'test', which checks only that the named file still declares the pinned method - a gutted or @Disabled body satisfies it. The sibling probe adr-0046-token-refusal-asserted is what pins the assertion itself.

The fail-closed test still ASSERTS a refusal, not merely that a method by that name exists: ApiSecurityFiltersTest expects an IllegalStateException from the production constructor. Gutting the body to a no-op keeps adr-0046-token-fails-closed green and fails this one.
probes.note: Deliberately no 'expect' count: the claim is 'at least one refusal is still asserted', not a fixed number of cases, so adding a case must not fail the gate. Pairs with the kind:test probe, which pins the method NAME; this one pins that the method still asserts something.

probes.premise: The context ladder steps down when a rung produces a hard, detectable launch abort. llama-server defaults '--fit on' and that pass MAXIMIZES rather than fits (measured: 242,944 tokens / 4 GB KV with -c omitted), so a memory-adjusting heuristic running beside an explicit -c could absorb the very abort the step-down reads as its signal. The launch therefore passes '-fit off' unconditionally. Drop that flag and ADR-0047's step-down premise becomes an inference again rather than a property of the launch line.
probes.note: expect 1 is the population, not a ratchet: memoryPlanFlags is the single argv site for the memory-plan block, and LlamaServerLaunchFlagsTest asserts the FULL ordered argv rather than 'contains'. The pattern spans a line wrap in the source, which \\s* absorbs.

probes.premise: The window is contributed at its honest ordinal, never promoted into a system property where the resolver reads it as 'jvm_arg' (500) and effective-config reports a GUI default as an operator override. The promotion helper is deleted, not merely unused; resurrecting it under any name re-opens the precedence lie this ADR exists to close.
probes.note: Scoped to Java sources across all modules: the symbol must not come back in the controller, in a helper, or in a test that would keep a resurrected path green. Docs and tempdocs may still NAME the retired helper (retire-with-a-sweep asks for 'delete or label'), which is why the probe does not scan docs/.

probes.premise: The rung the Head contributes at ordinal 150 and the rung LlamaServerOps actually launches are the same number, and the backend (GPU layers vs -ngl 0) is what selects the top rung. ContextWindowPolicyTest#autoTopRungByBackend pins that identity. HONEST LIMIT: kind 'test' checks only that the file still declares the member — a gutted body satisfies it; the sibling probe adr-0047-fit-off-explicit and the exact-argv assertion in LlamaServerLaunchFlagsTest are what pin behaviour.

Every prompt-side budget is min(fraction x inputBudget, cap) computed per request from the LIVE window — not a constant, and not a static final resolved at class-init. ContextBudget is the single authority; the four capped accessors (section target, external context, read page, tool result) each derive from inputBudget.
probes.note: expect 4 is the population, not a growth ratchet: there are exactly four capped fractions in the design table (ADR-0047 section 6). The uncapped fifth quantity, hierarchicalThreshold(), IS the input budget and so has no 'capped(' call — adding a fifth CAPPED budget is a design change that should re-open this ADR's table, which is why the count is pinned rather than left open.

probes.premise: The hierarchical summarizer's split threshold is the live input budget, not a window-blind literal. The retired HIERARCHICAL_THRESHOLD_TOKENS = 5000 sent a 4999-token document single-pass into a 4096-token window whose honest input budget was ~2300; its return in any form would restore that.
probes.note: Scoped to the one file that owned the constant. The WHY comment at its old site deliberately names the retired LITERAL (5000) and not the symbol, so the label retire-with-a-sweep asks for does not fight the probe.

probes.premise: Crash isolation IS the persistent child pool. If PersistentExtractionSandbox disappears (folded back into the Worker JVM, or replaced by a per-file spawn), ADR-0048's first decision is no longer implemented and a looping parser takes the Worker down again.
probes.note: expect 1 is the population: one class declaration in its own file, not a ratchet.

probes.premise: The duty cycle REPLACED the pause; it did not sit beside it. isUserActive/signalUserActivity returning anywhere in main source would mean the pause is back, and a pause is a full stop under a continuous query loop (measured: 0 docs/s).
probes.note: Matches the DECLARATION, not the identifier: both names survive in javadoc prose that explains what the duty cycle replaced (ForegroundLoad, IndexingPacing), and deleting that prose would lose the history. The property is that no such method exists to call.

probes.premise: The eval-only escape hatch justsearch.eval.disable_breath_holding was deleted with the pause. Its return would mean measurement and production diverge again — and 885 [R1] showed the hatch could never even reach the Worker, so it measured nothing.

The duty-cycle claim is a live property, not a stubbed one: indexing must be throttled rather than stopped while real foreground searches are in flight, and status/health polling must not throttle it at all. Retargeted at lane F stage A item A12 — the witness kept its subject and both arms, and moved from ChaosSuiteTest$TimeLordTests (an opt-in systemTest tier that had been unreachable since item A9 deleted the gRPC server the spawned Worker published a port on) to a test that composes the same index half in-process and runs on every build. The witness is stronger, not weaker: in one JVM it can also assert the gauge itself (ForegroundLoad.startedTotal), which the wire test could not see.

NARROWED by the ADR's 2026-09-07 amendment. ForegroundLoad is a worker-services type, so the TYPE survives a Head/Worker merge -- but its producer does not, and a re-homed producer is a new integration rather than a move. This test pins the gauge's BALANCE across ok/error/cancel closes: every increment has a decrement. That is a real property and it is not the one that broke, because an always-balanced counter that is never incremented is perfectly balanced. The 'is it fed at all' half is adr-0048-foreground-gauge-has-a-live-producer.
probes.note: RETARGETED, not weakened, by lane F stage A item A9 (2026-09-07). The premise is unchanged and is now MORE true: ADR-0048 predicted that the interceptor was the throwaway adapter and that the gauge would survive the Head/Worker merge, and A9 is where the adapter was thrown away. The named file moved with the producer — ForegroundLoadInterceptorTest went with the interceptor; ForegroundLoadGateTest pins the same balance property (ok / exception / cancellation / Error, plus never-negative under concurrency) on ForegroundLoadGate, which is now the gauge's only producer. Per this register's own amendment rule the probe was not edited to make a violation pass: the violation is that the pin's SUBJECT was deleted by a decision this ADR anticipated.

probes.premise: The duty cycle needs the gauge to be FED, not merely balanced. Between lane F item A6 and the 2026-09-07 fix it was not: ForegroundLoadGate mirrored the interceptor's gRPC method names while the executor seam passes lower-camel operation labels, so the gauge read zero on every call and indexing never yielded to a waiting search. Both existing suites stayed green because both fed the gate the vocabulary the gate itself declared. A gauge probe that does not enter through the seam's real caller tests the gauge against itself.
probes.note: Added by the lane F stage A A6-A9 review (2026-09-07). The pinned assertion is that a real client.search(...) through EngineRoot moves ForegroundLoad.startedTotal. It lives inside the full boot test deliberately: the defect was that the seam's real caller never reached the gate, and a test that builds its own gate cannot observe that. This is the assertion that failed 'expected: <1> but was: <0>' on its first run.

probes.premise: A permanently failing file must reach a VISIBLE terminal state rather than silently ceasing to be retried. Losing this constant means the ladder has no terminus and the invisible-abandonment failure returns.
probes.note: The declaration site, not every mention: the constant has three readers in the same file, so a bare identifier count would be a refactor-fragile ratchet rather than a presence property.

probes.premise: on_demand was REJECTED by its own measurement and ships opt-in. If the default flips to on_demand without a clean re-measure, the ADR's cadence decision has been reversed silently.
probes.note: expect 1 is the population: one enum declaration. The pattern pins the three policy-bearing leading arguments, including the literal default, while allowing orthogonal declaration metadata after them; a default flip still fails the probe.
